mainTopic: רבי יהודה and labels (כתיבה) in the מקדש: the single כן, the thirteen שופרות, the missing חטאת box, and רבי יהודה's rejection of ברירה.
overview: The גמרא claims that רבי יהודה does not trust written labels (כתיבה) to prevent mix-ups. Its proof is his view that the blood of יום הכיפורים had only one stand (כן): if labels worked, two labeled stands would have been fine. A ברייתא challenges this. In רבי יהודה's own view, the מקדש had thirteen labeled collection boxes (שופרות), but no box for obligatory חטאת birds. רב דימי explains that the missing box is a rabbinic decree (גזירה) because of a חטאת whose owner has died. The גמרא objects that we normally presume an owner is alive. It answers that in a shared box, some donor's death is certain. Why not simply destroy four זוזים and permit the rest? Because רבי יהודה does not accept ברירה. The גמרא then asks for the source of this. It begins quoting a משנה about buying wine from כותים just before שבת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does not rely on writing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that רבי יהודה does not accept written labels as a way to prevent mix-ups.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי יהודה] does not hold of writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating its claim: רבי יהודה does not trust written labels to keep sacrificial items from being mixed up. It is about to prove this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that, for רבי יהודה, writing "this one is for X" on a container is not enough protection against error. The next lines bring the source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: Writing, meaning a written label used to tell items apart
He does not hold of / does not accept

phrases.english: [Rabbi Yehuda] does not accept writing.
phrases.notes: He does not rely on written labels to prevent errors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a claim begun at the end of the previous amud (55a).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה does not rely on written labels to prevent mix-ups.

steps.title: Proof from the single blood stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רבי יהודה's view that there was only one כן for the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה says, there was only one stand there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה as its source: רבי יהודה says only one stand (כן) was used to hold the bowls of blood on יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול puts down the bull's blood and the goat's blood at different points in the עבודה. רבי יהודה says there was just one stand, so only one bowl could rest there at a time. The גמרא will argue that this choice shows he distrusts labels.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A stand or pedestal on which a bowl of blood was placed
Only

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה שָׁם אֶלָּא כַּן אֶחָד בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: There was only one stand there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the claim in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יהודה does not rely on writing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in which רבי יהודה says there was only one כן.

steps.title: Why not two stands?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה did not allow two stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two — what is the reason not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה rejects two stands, one for each kind of blood. This question sets up the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two stands would seem easier, since each blood would have its own place. Asking why this was rejected will expose רבי יהודה's underlying worry.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Why not two [stands]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the reason behind the משנה just cited.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה rejects having two stands.

steps.title: Because they could be switched
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that two stands might be confused with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that with two stands, the כהן might mix them up and take the goat's blood instead of the bull's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is a mix-up (חילוף) between the two bloods. With only one stand, only one bowl sits there at a time, so no switch is possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of
That they get switched or confused

phrases.english: Because they would be switched.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two stands might be confused with each other.

steps.title: Why not label the two stands?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a simple fix: make two stands and write on each which blood it holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us make two and write on them which is for the bull and which is for the goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes an obvious solution: label the stands. This prepares the conclusion that רבי יהודה must not trust labels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If labels worked, they would remove the worry about a mix-up. Since רבי יהודה still insists on one stand, he must think labels are not reliable enough.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us make
And let us write
Which one

phrases.english: But let us make two
and write on them
which is for the bull and which is for the goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason in step 4 by offering a fix.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that two stands would be switched.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Written labels would prevent a switch, so the worry alone should not rule out two stands.

steps.title: Therefore רבי יהודה does not trust labels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה does not rely on writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהודה does not accept writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion: since רבי יהודה did not simply use labeled stands, he must not trust written labels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the claim from step 1, now proven. רבי יהודה's refusal to use labeled stands shows that, to him, labels do not prevent errors.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; therefore it must be

steps.whatToRemember: According to this line of reasoning, רבי יהודה does not rely on written labels (כתיבה) to prevent mix-ups. His single כן is the proof.

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
he does not accept writing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֵית לֵיהּ כְּתִיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes from the failed suggestion in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה does not rely on written labels to prevent mix-ups.

steps.title: Challenge: thirteen labeled collection boxes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the מקדש had thirteen boxes, each with a written label.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: There were thirteen collection horns (שופרות) in the מקדש, and on them was written: new שקלים, old שקלים, nests (קינין), young birds for עולה, wood, frankincense (לבונה), gold for the כפורת, and six for נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an objection from a ברייתא: the money boxes (שופרות) in the מקדש were told apart by written labels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each box held money for a different purpose, and only the writing on it showed which was which. The next step will show that this is רבי יהודה's view, which seems to contradict the claim that he does not trust labels.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
Horn-shaped collection boxes
Shekels
Nests; pairs of birds for offerings
Voluntary offering

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שׁוֹפָרוֹת הָיוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: They objected: There were thirteen collection horns in the Temple,
and it was written on them:
New shekels, and old shekels,
and nests, and young birds for burnt-offerings,
and wood, and frankincense,
and gold for the Ark cover,
and six for free-will offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שׁוֹפָרוֹת הָיוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי יהודה does not rely on writing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The boxes were told apart only by their written labels, so the מקדש did rely on writing.

steps.title: The ברייתא explains the labels — רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains each label, says all the bird boxes were for עולות, and attributes this to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: New שקלים: these are the שקלים of each year. Old שקלים: one who did not give last year gives the next year. Nests (קינין): these are turtledoves. Young birds for עולה: these are pigeons. And all of them are עולות — the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what each label meant and ends by saying this is רבי יהודה's opinion. This completes the objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the labeled system is רבי יהודה's view, he does seem to rely on writing, which contradicts step 6. He also says both bird boxes held only עולות, so there was no box for obligatory חטאת birds. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: Last year
Turtledoves
Young pigeons
Burnt-offerings

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two bird boxes. Both held money for עולות only. One was for turtledoves and one for pigeons. According to רבי יהודה, neither was for חטאת birds.

phrases.aramaic: תִּקְלִין חַדְתִּין — אֵלּוּ שְׁקָלִים שֶׁל כׇּל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה,
phrases.english: New shekels — these are the shekels of each and every year,
old shekels —
one who did not give a shekel last year
gives it in the following year.
Nests — these are turtledoves,
young birds for burnt-offerings — these are pigeons,
and all of them are burnt-offerings; these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and attributes it to רבי יהודה, which completes the objection.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה does not rely on writing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה himself describes a labeled system of boxes, so he does rely on writing.

steps.title: רב דימי: a decree because of a sin-offering whose owners died
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports from ארץ ישראל that there was no חטאת bird box because of a rabbinic decree about a חטאת whose owners have died.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: They say in the West, it is a decree because of a sin-offering whose owners have died.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי explains why רבי יהודה had no box for obligatory חטאת birds. The reason was a rabbinic decree (גזירה), not a problem with labels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת whose owner has died may not be offered. It is left to die. If many people's money for חטאת birds were pooled in one box and one donor died, his money would be mixed in and could not be used. So the missing box comes from this concern, not from distrust of writing.

keyTerms.meaning: When [he] came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
A rabbinic decree
A sin-offering whose owners have died; it may not be offered and is left to die

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the reason for the missing חטאת box away from the question of writing. That allows the sugya to keep רבי יהודה's labeled boxes in place.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
They say in the West:
It is a decree because of a sin-offering whose owners have died.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אֲמַר: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יהודה excluded a חטאת bird box, in response to the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Provides a different reason for רבי יהודה's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's ruling might seem tied to the question of mix-ups and labels.
steps.terutzMaskana: The missing חטאת box is a rabbinic decree because a donor might die.

steps.title: Do we really worry the owner died?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב דימי from a משנה: a חטאת sent from overseas is offered on the assumption that its owner is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we worry about this? But we learned: one who sends his sin-offering from overseas — they offer it on the presumption that he is alive!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב דימי's answer. A משנה shows that we normally do not worry that the owner of a חטאת has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone far away sends his חטאת to the מקדש, and it is offered even though he could have died in the meantime. We assume he is alive (חזקה). So why would the חכמים worry about a donor's death in the bird box?

keyTerms.meaning: And do we worry [about this]?
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Overseas; a faraway land
On the presumption that he is alive

steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי says the missing box is a גזירה because a donor might die, but the משנה says we presume the owner of a חטאת is alive. The next step answers this by limiting the decree to a death that is certain.

phrases.english: And are we concerned [about that]?
But didn't we learn:
One who sends his sin-offering from overseas —
they offer it on the presumption that he is alive!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב דימי's answer in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that there is a גזירה because of a חטאת whose owners have died.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that we presume the owner of a חטאת is alive, so the worry about his death should not lead to a decree.

steps.title: The concern is a חטאת whose owner has certainly died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the משנה about a חטאת sent from overseas. The decree is not about a doubtful case. It is about a case where we know for sure that some owner has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the decree is because of a חטאת whose owner has certainly died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes how it understands רב דימי's reason. The worry is about a sure death, not a possible one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in Step 10 says we assume a single owner is alive when we are only unsure. A shared box is different. Over time many people put money in, so it is certain that at least one of them has died. Money for a חטאת whose owner has certainly died must be destroyed, and once it is mixed into the box, all the money becomes a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This signals a corrected explanation.
A sin-offering whose owner has died. It cannot be brought and must be left to die or be destroyed.
Certainly. Something known for sure, as opposed to a doubt (סָפֵק).

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not contradict the overseas משנה. That משנה is about a doubt concerning one person. Here, with many donors, a death is certain.

phrases.english: Rather: because of a sin-offering
whose owner has certainly died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מִשּׁוּם חַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ וַדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10 by redefining the decree as covering a certain death, not a doubtful one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree is about a doubtful death, which would contradict the משנה that presumes the owner is alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree is about a death that is certain in a pooled box, so the presumption of life does not apply.

steps.title: Why not destroy four זוזים and permit the rest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a fix. Take out the value of one bird offering, four זוזים, and throw it into water. Then say that this was the dead person's money, and the rest is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us select four זוזים and throw them into the water, and these other coins will be permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for a decree. It proposes a simple way to solve the mixed-money problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the problem is only that one donor's money is mixed in, removing one offering's worth should fix it. We would say afterwards that the coins we threw away were the forbidden ones. This idea depends on looking back and deciding after the fact which coins were which.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us select or separate.
זוזים, silver coins. Four of them was the price of a bird offering.
Let us throw them into the water, destroying them.
They will become permitted.

phrases.english: But let us select four zuz
and throw them into the water,
and these remaining coins will be permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 11 by proposing a practical fix that would make the decree unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a certain dead owner's money ruins the whole box, so no חטאת box could exist.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing and destroying one offering's value should isolate the forbidden money and free the rest.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does not accept ברירה
steps.stepSummary: The fix does not work for רבי יהודה, because he does not accept ברירה. We cannot decide afterwards that certain coins were the forbidden ones all along.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה does not hold of ברירה (retroactive clarification).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proposed fix. It works only if you accept ברירה, and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throwing away four זוזים and calling them the dead man's money is a retroactive choice. רבי יהודה holds that a later choice cannot clarify what was true earlier. So the remaining money stays mixed and forbidden, and the decree against a חטאת box stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of; he does not accept.
Retroactive clarification. A later choice shows what was designated from the start.

steps.whyThisMatters: ברירה is a major concept across ש״ס. This step ties the box decree to רבי יהודה's general position on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda does not accept retroactive clarification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by showing that its fix depends on ברירה, which רבי יהודה rejects.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting a premise based on the תנא's known view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Retroactive selection could free the remaining coins.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה rejects ברירה, so the coins cannot be freed this way.

steps.title: How do we know רבי יהודה rejects ברירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that רבי יהודה does not accept ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the claim it just made. This sets up the next step, where it starts bringing a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 stated רבי יהודה's view without proof. Now the גמרא wants a text where רבי יהודה clearly rejects ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? A request for a source.

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the claim made in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source proving that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה.

steps.title: A proposed source: buying wine from כותים before שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts bringing a possible source, a משנה about someone who buys untithed wine from כותים right before שבת. He declares that two לוגין, which he will separate later, are תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is from what we learned in the משנה: One who buys wine from the כותים on ערב שבת at nightfall may stand and say, 'Two לוגין that I will separate in the future are hereby תרומה'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה as a possible proof. The word 'אילימא' warns us this proof will probably be rejected, and the משנה continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the person names the תרומה now but picks the actual wine only later. That sounds like ברירה. On the next amud, the full משנה records רבי מאיר permitting this, while רבי יהודה (with רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון) forbids it. That is why it is relevant here. The 'If you say' opening suggests the גמרא will reject this source and look for a better one.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. It introduces a suggestion that usually gets rejected.
Samaritans. They were not trusted to tithe their produce properly.
At nightfall, just before שבת begins.
לוגין, a liquid measure.
The portion of produce given to a כהן.

steps.confusionAlert: This proof is not finished. The משנה continues into the next passage, and 'אילימא' signals that the גמרא will probably reject it.

phrases.english: If we say it is from that which we learned in a mishna:
One who buys wine from among the Samaritans,
on Shabbat eve at nightfall,
may stand and say:
phrases.notes: He has no time to actually separate the portions before שבת.

phrases.english: Two log that I will separate in the future
are hereby teruma.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues on the next amud with more separations and רבי יהודה's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מֵהָא דִּתְנַן: הַלּוֹקֵחַ יַיִן מִבֵּין הַכּוּתִיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering Step 14 by proposing a משנה as the source.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about buying wine from כותים on ערב שבת, where portions are designated now and separated later.
